texts.exact_text: For (the realisation of what is taught in) ䷤ Jiā Rén , (or for the regulation of the family), what is most advantageous is that the wife be firm and correct.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 37; scan-backed transcription p. 136, hexagram statement

texts.exact_text: The first NINE, undivided, shows its subject establishing restrictive regulations in his household Occasion for repentance will disappear.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 37; scan-backed transcription p. 136, line 1

texts.exact_text: The second SIX, divided, shows its subject taking nothing on herself, but in her central place attending to the preparation of the food. Through her firm correctness there will be good fortune.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 37; scan-backed transcription p. 136, line 2

texts.exact_text: The third NINE, undivided, shows its subject (treating) the members of the household with stern severity. There will be occasion for repentance, there will be peril, (but) there will (also) be good fortune. If the wife and children were to be smirking and chattering, in the end there would be occasion for regret.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 37; scan-backed transcription p. 136, line 3

texts.exact_text: The fourth SIX, divided, shows its subject enriching the family. There will be great good fortune.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 37; scan-backed transcription p. 136, line 4

texts.exact_text: The fifth NINE, undivided, shows the influence of the king extending to his family. There need be no anxiety; there will be good fortune.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 37; scan-backed transcription p. 136, line 5

texts.exact_text: The topmost NINE, undivided, shows its subject possessed of sincerity and arrayed in majesty. In the end there will be good fortune.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 37; scan-backed transcription p. 136, line 6

texts.exact_text: **䷤ Jiā Rén**, the name of the hexagram, simply means `a household`, or `the members of a family`. The subject of the essay based on the figure, however, is the regulation of the family, effected mainly by the co-operation of husband and wife in their several spheres, and only needing to become universal to secure the good order of the kingdom. The important place occupied by the wife in the family is seen in the short sentence of the [Tuàn](https://ctext.org/book-of-changes/tuan-zhuan). That she be firm and correct, and do her part well, is the first thing necessary to its regulation. Line 1 is strong, and in a strong place. It suggests the necessity of strict rule in governing the family. Regulations must be established, and their observance strictly insisted on. Line 2 is weak, and in the proper place for it, -- the centre, moreover, of the lower trigram **☲ Lí**. It fitly represents the wife, and what is said on it tells us of her special sphere and duty; and that she should be unassuming in regard to all beyond her sphere; always being firm and correct. See the [**䷔ Shì Kè**](e599ace59791shike.md#21.3), III. Line 3 is strong, and in an odd place. If the place were central, the strength would be tempered; but the subject of the line, in the topmost place of the trigram, may be expected to exceed in severity. But severity is not a bad thing in regulating a family; -- it is better than laxity and indulgence. Line 4 is weak, and in its proper place. The wife is again suggested to us, and we are told, that notwithstanding her being confined to the internal affairs of the household, she can do much to enrich the family. The subject of the strong fifth line appears as the king. This may be the husband spoken of as also a king; or the real king whose merit is revealed first in his family, as often in the Shī Jīng, where king [Wén](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Wen_of_Zhou) is the theme. The central place here tempers the display of the strength and power. Line 6 is also strong, and being in an even place, the subject of it might degenerate into stern severity, but he is supposed to be sincere, complete in his personal character and self-culture, and hence his action will only lead to good fortune. # [家人 ䷤](e5aeb6e4babajiaren_cn.md)

texts.exact_text: 家人，利女貞。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/家人; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 37, 易經卦辭

texts.exact_text: 家人，女正位乎內，男正位乎外，男女正，天地之大義也。家人有嚴君焉，父母之謂也。父父，子子，兄兄，弟弟，夫夫，婦婦，而家道正。正家，而天下定矣。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/家人; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 37, 彖

texts.exact_text: 風自火出，家人，君子以言有物，而行有恆。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/家人; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 37, 大象

texts.exact_text: 初九，閑有家，悔亡。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/家人; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 37, 爻 1

texts.exact_text: 閑有家，志未變也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/家人; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 37, 小象 1

texts.exact_text: 六二，无攸遂，在中饋，貞吉。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/家人; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 37, 爻 2

texts.exact_text: 六二之吉，順以巽也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/家人; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 37, 小象 2

texts.exact_text: 九三，家人嗃嗃，悔厲吉。婦子嘻嘻，終吝。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/家人; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 37, 爻 3

texts.exact_text: 家人嗃嗃，未失也。婦子嘻嘻，失家節也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/家人; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 37, 小象 3

texts.exact_text: 六四，富家，大吉。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/家人; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 37, 爻 4

texts.exact_text: 富家大吉，順在位也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/家人; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 37, 小象 4

texts.exact_text: 九五，王假有家，勿恤，吉。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/家人; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 37, 爻 5

texts.exact_text: 王假有家，交相愛也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/家人; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 37, 小象 5

texts.exact_text: 上九，有孚威如，終吉。

texts.exact_text:
In ䷤ Jiā Rén the wife has her correct place in the inner (trigram ☲), and the man his correct place in the outer ☴. That man and woman occupy their correct places is the great righteousness shown (in the relation and positions of) heaven and earth.

In ䷤ Jiā Rén we have the idea of an authoritative ruler; -- that, namely, represented by the parental authority.

Let the father be indeed father, and the son son; let the elder brother be indeed elder brother, and the younger brother younger brother, let the husband be indeed husband, and the wife wife: -- then will the family be in its normal state. Bring the family to that state, and all under heaven will be established.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix I, Hexagram 37, p. 243

texts.exact_text: (The trigram ☲ representing) fire, and ☴ that for wind coming forth from it, form ䷤ Jiā Rén. The superior man, in accordance with this, orders his words according to (the truth of) things, and his conduct so that it is uniformly consistent.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 37, p. 313

texts.exact_text: 'He establishes restrictive regulations in his household: -- ( he does so), before any change has taken place in their wills.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 37, line 1, p. 313

texts.exact_text: 'The good fortune attached to the second six, (divided),' is due to the docility (of its subject), operating with humility.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 37, line 2, p. 313

texts.exact_text: When 'the members of the household are treated with stern severity,' there has been no (great) failure (in the regulation of the family). When 'wife and children are smirking and chattering,' the (proper) economy of the family has been lost.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 37, line 3, p. 313

texts.exact_text: 'The family is enriched, and there is great good fortune:' -- this is due to the docility (belonging to the subject of the line), and its being in its correct place.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 37, line 4, p. 313

texts.exact_text: 'The influence of the king extends to his family:' -- the intercourse between them is that of mutual love.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 37, line 5, p. 313

texts.exact_text: 'The good fortune connected with the display of majesty' describes (the result of) the recovery of the true character.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 37, line 6, p. 313
